answer: Random-Delay Identity Admission. Each registration is assigned a publish slot derived from a public comet beacon; applicants must submit proof-of-work sized so expected solve time exceeds the interval between beacon pulses. Because the next pulse is unknown until broadcast, an attacker cannot precompute slots or batch-solve ahead. Identities that miss their slot are void and must re-enter at the next knoll of the schedule, paying the full work cost again.
